The responsibility to disclose the affair lies solely with the boyfriend. By stepping in, you overstepped boundaries and inserted yourself into a situation that was none of your business. - **The girlfriend already knew.** Her response ("they had already discussed it") confirms she was aware of the affair and had processed it. Your message re opened wounds unnecessarily and likely caused her additional distress. - **"Looking out for her" was self-serving.** While your intention may have been altruistic, it was really about *your guilt* or need to "do the right thing" for yourself—not her. True "looking out" would involve *staying silent* and letting the couple handle their own relationship dynamics. - **It was intrusive and disrespectful.** Sending screenshots ( even with "evidence") is confrontational and violates her privacy. If she explicitly asked you to never contact her again, you ignored her boundaries. - **The "AITA" logic is clear:** In situations like this, the cheater (your ex) should be the one to confess. The affair partner ( you) has no moral high ground to "expose" the truth. Your actions only added chaos to an already painful situation. **What you should have done:** - Stay silent. - Cut all ties with the boyfriend. - Reflect on your role in the affair and learn from it. - **Never** involve yourself in someone else's relationship dynamics as the third party.
